Introducing Model Y Long Wheelbase – now available in the US & Puerto Rico

A 3-row, 6-seat configuration that brings exceptional interior space with ample headroom & legroom for all passengers

0-60 in 4.4 seconds
325 miles of range

– Front row: Heated/ventilated seats w/ powered thigh cushion
– Second row: Heated/ventilated captain seats w/ powered armrests & one‑touch fold
– Third row: Heated seats w/ power recline, one‑touch fold & child seat anchors

–  Improved airflow, increased efficiency & more range

– 89 cu ft of trunk space: with 6 passengers, trunk still fits a 28" and 20" suitcase each, plus frunk holds an additional 20" suitcase. Oversized items like snowboards and bikes also fit easily

– Engineered for safety w/ seat belts & side air bag optimized for second & third row

– Upgraded acoustic glass & suspension to minimize road noise

– Adaptive damping for a smooth, stable ride

– Staggered tires for enhanced grip

– Larger tailgate for better rear visibility & bigger windows overall to deliver great views from every seat

– 16" first row & 8” second row touchscreens + 19-speaker immersive Tesla Audio

– Upgraded 50W wireless charging pads w/ active cooling & charging ports for all other seats

– FSD Supervised & integrated Grok AI

— https://nitter.net/Tesla/status/2072450928087900404#m

Tesla Insurance is on track to launch soon in Washington state, as the company has filed for a new auto insurance program in the state.

The proposed start date is September 1, 2026. The program will have two safety scores: Safety Score and Safety Score with FSD (Supervised).

This would be the 16th U.S. state to get Tesla Insurance.

Even when we received dozens of replies and comments throughout the year that V14 Lite didn’t exist or wasn’t being worked on, we held firm with our timelines and speculations.

We ask that you once again trust in us, and we’re eager for V14 Lite on our 2018 Model 3 as well.

As for AI3 vehicles outside of North America, this will take some time. We’d give a very rough estimate of late August to early September for the first expansion.

Give the @Tesla_AI team just a bit more patience for this final stretch. We know you’ve been waiting a long time.

The update being released just to early-access customer vehicles may feel performative, but they are still customers nonetheless.

We’ve seen vehicles in the United States, Canada, and Mexico receive V14 Lite.

We expect additional waves to follow before the second week of July.

We’ve been confidently sharing our expectations on the V14 Lite launch for months, and the current deployment matches what we’ve echoed.

As with any major release, expect very little movement after the initial wave for 1-3 weeks. More waves soon, but may require point releases.


Tesla Tidbits (@teslatidbits)

Not looking good for any wide release for the initial version.  Exactly ONE vehicle has 2026.20.5.1 on the @teslascope service, getting it Monday.  Even pilot releases got better initial spread when we used to get consistent updates.

Makes me feel like they shoved it out the door to say they met their deadline and get their publicity from the big influencers while the rest of us peasants continue to wait.
